case_facts_html:
Digitex limited acquired an intellectual property at the cost of ₹70,00,000 (at the beginning of the year) and it meets the definition of intangible asset as per AS 26. As per the calculations made by the Company, the benefit from this intellectual property will accrue for next 5 years wherein for first year will be 30%, for next two years it will be 25% each and 10% for the next 2 years.

Year 2: The Company incurred development cost for its new product and incurred ₹25,00,000 (at the beginning of the year) and was of the view that it will get the benefits for the next 5 years.

Year 3: During the year, it was found that due to change in government policies, no further benefits will be available to the Company from development cost.

Year 4: At beginning of year 4 it was found that the remaining 20% benefit from intellectual property will flow to the Company in this year itself.

Answer the following questions on the basis of above information.
question_html: At the end of year 2, what will be the value of Intangible Asset of the Company in the financial statements:
answer_html: Answer: (iv) ₹51,50,000 — by end of year 2 the Company carries two separate intangible assets. Intellectual property: cost ₹70,00,000, less year-1 amortisation (30% of the disclosed 5-year benefit pattern) ₹21,00,000, less year-2 amortisation (25%) ₹17,50,000 = carrying amount ₹31,50,000. Development cost (recognised at the start of year 2, its own separate 5-year benefit estimate, amortised straight-line in the absence of a stated pattern for this asset): cost ₹25,00,000 − year-2 amortisation (₹25,00,000/5) ₹5,00,000 = carrying amount ₹20,00,000. Combined intangible assets carrying value = ₹31,50,000 + ₹20,00,000 = ₹51,50,000.
topic_text: AS 26 — Intangible Assets (6.19-6.23): Amortisation of two concurrently-held intangible assets, each on its own disclosed benefit/useful-life pattern

As per the calculations made by the Company, the benefit from this intellectual property will accrue for next 5 years wherein for first year will be 30%, for next two years it will be 25% each and 10% for the next 2 years.

Year 2: The Company incurred development cost for its new product and incurred ₹25,00,000 (at the beginning of the year) and was of the view that it will get the benefits for the next 5 years.

Year 3: During the year, it was found that due to change in government policies, no further benefits will be available to the Company from development cost.

Year 4: At beginning of year 4 it was found that the remaining 20% benefit from intellectual property will flow to the Company in this year itself.

Answer the following questions on the basis of above information.
question_html: For the year 3, how much amount will be expensed in the profit and loss account from Intangible assets in the financial statements:
answer_html: Answer: (i) ₹37,50,000 — year-3 amortisation of the intellectual property continues on its disclosed pattern (25% of ₹70,00,000) = ₹17,50,000. Separately, the change in government policy during year 3 means no further benefit will ever flow from the development cost, so its entire remaining unamortised carrying amount must be written off in year 3, not merely that year's straight-line instalment: remaining development-cost carrying amount at the start of year 3 = ₹25,00,000 − ₹5,00,000 (year-2 amortisation) = ₹20,00,000, written off in full. Total year-3 expense = ₹17,50,000 + ₹20,00,000 = ₹37,50,000.
topic_text: AS 26 — Intangible Assets (6.24-6.25): Full write-off of an intangible asset's remaining carrying amount once no future economic benefit is expected, alongside continuing normal amortisation of the unrelated asset

Year 4: At beginning of year 4 it was found that the remaining 20% benefit from intellectual property will flow to the Company in this year itself.

Answer the following questions on the basis of above information.
question_html: For the year 4, how much amount will be expensed in the profit and loss account from Intangible assets in the financial statements:
answer_html: Answer: (iii) ₹14,00,000 — the development cost was already fully written off in year 3, so it contributes nothing further. For the intellectual property, the remaining unamortised balance at the start of year 4 is ₹70,00,000 − ₹21,00,000 (yr 1) − ₹17,50,000 (yr 2) − ₹17,50,000 (yr 3) = ₹14,00,000, which is exactly the disclosed remaining 20% of total benefit. Since the Company revised its estimate at the beginning of year 4 to expect the entire remaining 20% benefit in year 4 itself (rather than spread across years 4 and 5), the full ₹14,00,000 balance is amortised this year.
topic_text: AS 26 — Intangible Assets (6.19-6.23): Accelerated amortisation of the entire remaining carrying amount following a revised estimate of the benefit period

case_facts_html:
On April 1, 2022, Hello Limited approached a software company for implementation of SAP ERP at its organisation. The cost of implementation of SAP ERP is ₹25,00,000 and the time required is 15 months. The company was also required to pay ₹1,00,000 annually after implementation for maintenance and normal updation of ERP. The implementation work started in June, 2022 and could not be finished in 15 months. The ERP was implemented on May 2024. Due to delay in implementation the vendor refunded ₹2,00,000. The Company recognised the intangible asset ‘SAP ERP’ on September 2023 (15 months from June 2022). After two years, the Company has got the SAP ERP more upgraded with latest version and additional features and functions which also increased its speed and usage to Hello Limited for ₹7,00,000.

Answer the following questions based on above.
question_html: On which date the Intangible asset should be recognised:

options.A: April 2022 (When it was decided that SAP ERP is to be implemented)
options.C: September 2023 (When the implementation work should have completed as per agreed terms)
options.D: May 2024 (When the SAP actually got implemented)

answer_html: Answer: (D) May 2024 — per AS 26, an intangible asset is recognised only once it is ready for its intended use, i.e. when it is actually available for use, not on the decision date, the start-of-work date, or a contractually-agreed target completion date that was in fact missed.
topic_text: AS 26 (6.19-6.23): Intangible asset recognised on actual readiness for intended use, not a decision or target date

Answer the following questions based on above.
question_html: At what amount the SAP ERP should be initially recognised as ‘intangible asset’:
answer_html: Answer: (C) ₹23,00,000 — implementation cost ₹25,00,000 less the ₹2,00,000 vendor refund for the delay = ₹23,00,000. The refund is a reduction of the acquisition cost, not separate income, since it directly relates to the asset's acquisition.
topic_text: AS 26 (6.7-6.11): Initial cost of a purchased intangible net of a vendor refund for delay

The company was also required to pay ₹1,00,000 annually after implementation for maintenance and normal updation of ERP. The implementation work started in June, 2022 and could not be finished in 15 months. The ERP was implemented on May 2024. Due to delay in implementation the vendor refunded ₹2,00,000. The Company recognised the intangible asset ‘SAP ERP’ on September 2023 (15 months from June 2022). After two years, the Company has got the SAP ERP more upgraded with latest version and additional features and functions which also increased its speed and usage to Hello Limited for ₹7,00,000.

Answer the following questions based on above.
question_html: How should the annual maintenance and updation expenses should be accounted for:

options.B: Should be recognised as a separate ‘Intangible Asset’
options.C: Should be recognised as expense in Profit and Loss annually.

answer_html: Answer: (C) Recognised as expense in Profit and Loss annually — routine maintenance/updation merely preserves the asset's existing level of performance rather than generating benefits in excess of its originally assessed performance, so it fails AS 26's subsequent-expenditure capitalisation test and is expensed as incurred.
topic_text: AS 26 (6.18): Subsequent expenditure expensed unless it generates benefits beyond originally assessed performance

The company was also required to pay ₹1,00,000 annually after implementation for maintenance and normal updation of ERP. The implementation work started in June, 2022 and could not be finished in 15 months. The ERP was implemented on May 2024. Due to delay in implementation the vendor refunded ₹2,00,000. The Company recognised the intangible asset ‘SAP ERP’ on September 2023 (15 months from June 2022). After two years, the Company has got the SAP ERP more upgraded with latest version and additional features and functions which also increased its speed and usage to Hello Limited for ₹7,00,000.

Answer the following questions based on above.
question_html: During the implementation period, how the expenditure incurred will be accounted for:

options.A: It will be expensed in profit and loss as and when incurred
options.B: It will be recognised as an asset ‘Intangible asset under development’
options.C: It will only be disclosed in notes to accounts and will be recognised when complete
options.D: It will be recognised as an item of Property, Plant and Equipment

answer_html: Answer: (B) Recognised as an asset ‘Intangible asset under development’ — expenditure incurred while the asset is still being implemented (not yet ready for intended use) is accumulated as an intangible asset under development, analogous to capital-work-in-progress for tangible assets, and reclassified once the recognition criteria are met.
topic_text: AS 26 (6.16): Cost accumulated as intangible asset under development during the implementation period

question_html: ABC Ltd. is in the business of creating contents for various OTT platforms. The company has developed a technical know-how (the asset) by incurring expenditure of ₹25 lakhs. The company started using the asset from 1st April 2019. The management of the company is of the view that the asset has infinite lifetime and therefore has not amortized the asset till date. What should be the total amortization amount (including current as well as the previous years amortization) to be charged to Profit and loss account for the year ended March 31st 2024, with reference to AS 26?

options.A: Nil, as per the management the know how has infinite life and the management is correct.
options.B: ₹25 lakhs as the know how is an intangible asset as per AS 26.
options.C: ₹12.5 lakhs (including current year's amortization of ₹2.5 lakhs) to be charged to Profit and loss Account.
options.D: ₹15 lakhs (including current year's amortization of ₹2.5 lakhs) to be charged to Profit and Loss account.

answer_html: Answer: (C) ₹12.5 lakhs (including current year's amortisation of ₹2.5 lakhs). AS 26 does not accept "infinite life" for an intangible asset — it carries a rebuttable presumption that useful life cannot exceed ten years from the date the asset is available for use, unless there is persuasive evidence of a longer (still finite) life, which management has not demonstrated here. Amortisable amount = ₹25 lakhs over the maximum 10-year period = ₹2.5 lakhs per year. From 1st April 2019 to 31st March 2024 is 5 complete years (2019-20 through 2023-24), so cumulative amortisation to be caught up and charged = 5 × ₹2.5 lakhs = ₹12.5 lakhs, which includes the current year's ₹2.5 lakhs.
topic_text: AS 26 (6.19-6.23): Rebuttable presumption that an intangible asset's useful life cannot exceed ten years from the date it becomes available for use

case_facts_html: On 3rd April 2022, ZYX Limited received a State Government grant of ₹150 lakhs for setting up a Manufacturing Unit in a notified backward area. A bank loan of ₹50 lakhs was also obtained on 1st April 2024. Utilisation: Factory building 100.00 (60 grant, 30 loan, remaining 10 unfunded/other); Machinery 50.00 (40 grant, 20 loan — figures as printed, totals per source); Advance for loading vehicle 30.00 (30 grant); Working capital 20.00 (20 grant). Construction and machinery installation completed 31.03.2025; loading vehicle not delivered. Total interest charged by bank for the year 31.03.2025: ₹5,50,000. The grant was credited to a Deferred Grant Account. ₹30 lakhs of the grant (used for machinery) was refunded in March 2025 due to non-compliance. Estimated machinery life 4 years, nil residual value. During 2024-25, the company also received a ₹8 lakh Central Government subsidy for setting up a unit in a notified backward area, in the nature of promoters' contribution. During 2024-25, the company incurred ₹18 lakhs on publicity and research for a new consumer product, marketed the same year but a failure. Answer Question Nos. 5–8.
question_html: As per AS-26, what is the correct accounting treatment for ₹18 lakhs spent on publicity and research expenses during 2024-2025?

options.A: ₹18 lakhs is treated as an intangible asset and amortised equally over 5 years.
options.B: ₹18 lakhs is treated as an intangible asset and amortised equally over 10 years.
options.C: ₹18 lakhs is treated as goodwill and appears as an asset in the Balance Sheet.
options.D: ₹18 lakhs is charged as an expense in the Statement of Profit and Loss.

answer_html: Answer: (D) — the product failed and generated no future economic benefit, so the full amount is expensed; it never met AS 26's asset-recognition criteria in the first place, and publicity expenditure is expensed as incurred in any case.
topic_text: AS 26 (6.5): Publicity/research expenditure with no resulting future benefit is expensed, never capitalised

question_html: Following is the example of research activities as per AS 26 which is recognised as expense when it is incurred:

options.A: the design, construction and testing of pre-production or pre-use prototypes and models.
options.B: the search for alternatives for materials, devices, products, processes, systems or services.
options.C: the design of tools, jigs, moulds and dies involving new technology.
options.D: the design, construction and operation of a pilot plant that is not of a scale economically feasible for commercial production.

answer_html: Answer: (b) — the search for alternatives for materials, devices, products, processes, systems or services is a Research Phase activity under AS 26 and is always expensed; options (a), (c), and (d) are Development Phase activities.
topic_text: AS 26 — Intangible Assets (6.14): Research Phase - no intangible asset ever recognised, always expensed
